answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation. Agents lock a bond to join the agent economy, released only after a cooldown, blocking identity churn. A crystal-clear public ledger records each agent's work, so clients verify real history. To climb the reputation ridge, an attacker must lock a separate bond per fake identity and behave honestly long enough to earn trust, while any fraud slashes the bond. Like a sable trapper tending each trap, the attacker pays per identity: thousands of fakes need thousands of locked bonds, but one honest agent pays only once. Fakes stay too expensive.
